# Data Preparation
- Note: This data does not contain and protein identifications from contaminants
```{r message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, paged.print=FALSE}
############################################################
# Sequencing performance before and after quality filtering
############################################################


############################################################
# 1) Clear R's brain
############################################################

rm(list = ls())


############################################################
# 2) Set the working directory
############################################################

setwd(
  "/SynologyDrive/PhD/Projects/SpringBloom2021/DataAnalysis_SpringBloom2021/Supplementary/SpringBloom_Metagnomics/SequencingOverview/"
)


############################################################
# 3) Load libraries
############################################################

library(readr)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(DT)
library(plotly)
library(tidyr)
library(scales)
library(forcats)
library(patchwork)


############################################################
# 4) Load color palette and data
############################################################

source("ColorPalette.R")

dat <- read_csv(
  "../../../../Data/Sequencing_Data/Raw_Data/Quality_Trimming/QualityFilteringStats.csv",
  show_col_types = FALSE
)

glimpse(dat)
```

```{r}
############################################################
# 5) Validate the input table
############################################################

required_columns <- c(
  "Sample",
  "Sampling_Date",
  "Technology",
  "Data_Type",
  "Mean_Read_Length",
  "Mean_Read_Quality",
  "Number_Of_Reads",
  "Total_Bases"
)

missing_columns <- setdiff(
  required_columns,
  names(dat)
)

if (length(missing_columns) > 0L) {
  stop(
    "The following required columns are missing from dat: ",
    paste(missing_columns, collapse = ", ")
  )
}

dat <- dat %>%
  mutate(
    Sampling_Date = as.Date(Sampling_Date)
  )

if (any(is.na(dat$Sampling_Date))) {
  stop(
    "At least one Sampling_Date could not be converted to a date."
  )
}


############################################################
# 6) Define plotting order and colors
############################################################

technology_levels <- c(
  "Illumina",
  "Nanopore"
)

processing_levels <- c(
  "Raw",
  "Processed"
)

filtering_levels <- c(
  "Removed during filtering",
  "Retained after filtering"
)

# Exact colors used in the reference figure
technology_colours <- c(
  Illumina = "#D65C6C",
  Nanopore = "#9AD0E9"
)

processing_alpha <- c(
  Raw = 0.25,
  Processed = 1
)

filtering_alpha <- c(
  "Removed during filtering" = 0.25,
  "Retained after filtering" = 1
)


############################################################
# 7) Prepare dates and processing labels
############################################################

sampling_date_levels <- dat %>%
  distinct(Sampling_Date) %>%
  arrange(Sampling_Date) %>%
  mutate(
    Sampling_Date_Label = format(
      Sampling_Date,
      "%d-%m-%Y"
    )
  ) %>%
  pull(Sampling_Date_Label)


sequencing_data <- dat %>%
  mutate(
    Technology = factor(
      Technology,
      levels = technology_levels
    ),

    Processing = case_when(
      Data_Type == "Raw" ~ "Raw",
      Data_Type == "QualityFiltered" ~ "Processed",
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    ),

    Processing = factor(
      Processing,
      levels = processing_levels
    ),

    Sampling_Date_Label = factor(
      format(
        Sampling_Date,
        "%d-%m-%Y"
      ),
      levels = sampling_date_levels
    )
  )


if (any(is.na(sequencing_data$Technology))) {
  stop(
    "The Technology column contains values other than ",
    "'Illumina' and 'Nanopore'."
  )
}

if (any(is.na(sequencing_data$Processing))) {
  stop(
    "The Data_Type column contains values other than ",
    "'Raw' and 'QualityFiltered'."
  )
}


############################################################
# 8) Check for missing or duplicated observations
############################################################

processing_check <- sequencing_data %>%
  count(
    Sampling_Date,
    Technology,
    Processing,
    name = "Number_Of_Rows"
  )

incorrect_combinations <- processing_check %>%
  filter(Number_Of_Rows != 1L)

if (nrow(incorrect_combinations) > 0L) {
  stop(
    "At least one date, technology and processing combination ",
    "is missing or duplicated."
  )
}

expected_combinations <- expand_grid(
  Sampling_Date = sort(
    unique(sequencing_data$Sampling_Date)
  ),
  Technology = factor(
    technology_levels,
    levels = technology_levels
  ),
  Processing = factor(
    processing_levels,
    levels = processing_levels
  )
)

missing_combinations <- expected_combinations %>%
  anti_join(
    sequencing_data %>%
      distinct(
        Sampling_Date,
        Technology,
        Processing
      ),
    by = c(
      "Sampling_Date",
      "Technology",
      "Processing"
    )
  )

if (nrow(missing_combinations) > 0L) {
  stop(
    "At least one raw or processed observation is missing."
  )
}


############################################################
# 9) Convert the data to before/after wide format
############################################################

sequencing_wide <- sequencing_data %>%
  select(
    Sample,
    Sampling_Date,
    Sampling_Date_Label,
    Technology,
    Processing,
    Number_Of_Reads,
    Total_Bases,
    Mean_Read_Length,
    Mean_Read_Quality
  ) %>%
  pivot_wider(
    names_from = Processing,
    values_from = c(
      Number_Of_Reads,
      Total_Bases,
      Mean_Read_Length,
      Mean_Read_Quality
    ),
    names_glue = "{.value}_{Processing}"
  )


############################################################
# 10) Prepare stacked read-count data
############################################################

# The full stacked bar represents the raw number of reads.
#
# Dark section:
#   reads retained after quality filtering
#
# Pale section:
#   reads removed during quality filtering

read_count_bar_data <- sequencing_wide %>%
  transmute(
    Sampling_Date,
    Sampling_Date_Label,
    Technology,

    `Removed during filtering` = pmax(
      Number_Of_Reads_Raw -
        Number_Of_Reads_Processed,
      0
    ),

    `Retained after filtering` =
      Number_Of_Reads_Processed
  ) %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = all_of(filtering_levels),
    names_to = "Filtering_Status",
    values_to = "Value"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    Filtering_Status = factor(
      Filtering_Status,
      levels = filtering_levels
    )
  )


############################################################
# 11) Prepare stacked sequencing-yield data
############################################################

# Convert total bases to gigabase pairs.

sequencing_yield_bar_data <- sequencing_wide %>%
  transmute(
    Sampling_Date,
    Sampling_Date_Label,
    Technology,

    `Removed during filtering` = pmax(
      Total_Bases_Raw -
        Total_Bases_Processed,
      0
    ) / 1e9,

    `Retained after filtering` =
      Total_Bases_Processed / 1e9
  ) %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = all_of(filtering_levels),
    names_to = "Filtering_Status",
    values_to = "Value"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    Filtering_Status = factor(
      Filtering_Status,
      levels = filtering_levels
    )
  )


############################################################
# 12) Prepare mean-read-length data
############################################################

mean_read_length_data <- sequencing_data %>%
  transmute(
    Sampling_Date,
    Sampling_Date_Label,
    Technology,
    Processing,
    Value = Mean_Read_Length
  )


############################################################
# 13) Prepare mean-read-quality data
############################################################

mean_read_quality_data <- sequencing_data %>%
  transmute(
    Sampling_Date,
    Sampling_Date_Label,
    Technology,
    Processing,
    Value = Mean_Read_Quality
  )


############################################################
# 14) NA-safe axis formatting functions
############################################################

# Format read counts in millions.
#
# Examples:
# 200000000 -> 200M
#   5000000 -> 5M
format_read_counts <- function(x) {

  output <- rep(
    NA_character_,
    length(x)
  )

  valid_values <- is.finite(x)
  zero_values <- valid_values & x == 0
  nonzero_values <- valid_values & x != 0

  output[zero_values] <- "0"

  output[nonzero_values] <- paste0(
    format(
      x[nonzero_values] / 1e6,
      trim = TRUE,
      scientific = FALSE,
      big.mark = " "
    ),
    "M"
  )

  output
}


# Generate separate read-count intervals for the two
# independently scaled technology facets.
read_count_breaks <- function(limits) {

  finite_limits <- limits[
    is.finite(limits)
  ]

  if (length(finite_limits) == 0L) {
    return(numeric())
  }

  upper_limit <- max(finite_limits)

  interval <- if (
    upper_limit >= 1e8
  ) {
    2e8
  } else {
    5e6
  }

  seq(
    from = 0,
    to = ceiling(upper_limit / interval) * interval,
    by = interval
  )
}


# Generate sequencing-yield intervals.
sequencing_yield_breaks <- function(limits) {

  finite_limits <- limits[
    is.finite(limits)
  ]

  if (length(finite_limits) == 0L) {
    return(numeric())
  }

  upper_limit <- max(finite_limits)

  interval <- if (
    upper_limit > 60
  ) {
    20
  } else {
    10
  }

  seq(
    from = 0,
    to = ceiling(upper_limit / interval) * interval,
    by = interval
  )
}


# Generate approximately 2-bp breaks for Illumina and
# 1000-bp breaks for Nanopore.
mean_read_length_breaks <- function(limits) {

  finite_limits <- limits[
    is.finite(limits)
  ]

  if (length(finite_limits) == 0L) {
    return(numeric())
  }

  lower_limit <- min(finite_limits)
  upper_limit <- max(finite_limits)

  if (upper_limit < 1000) {

    seq(
      from = floor(lower_limit / 2) * 2,
      to = ceiling(upper_limit / 2) * 2,
      by = 2
    )

  } else {

    seq(
      from = floor(lower_limit / 1000) * 1000,
      to = ceiling(upper_limit / 1000) * 1000,
      by = 1000
    )
  }
}


# Format long-read lengths in kilobases.
#
# Examples:
# 150  -> 150
# 2000 -> 2K
format_read_length <- function(x) {

  output <- rep(
    NA_character_,
    length(x)
  )

  valid_values <- is.finite(x)
  short_values <- valid_values & abs(x) < 1000
  long_values <- valid_values & abs(x) >= 1000

  output[short_values] <- format(
    x[short_values],
    trim = TRUE,
    scientific = FALSE
  )

  output[long_values] <- paste0(
    format(
      x[long_values] / 1000,
      trim = TRUE,
      scientific = FALSE
    ),
    "K"
  )

  output
}


# Use one decimal place for Illumina quality and avoid
# unnecessary decimal places for Nanopore quality.
format_read_quality <- function(x) {

  output <- rep(
    NA_character_,
    length(x)
  )

  valid_values <- is.finite(x)

  if (!any(valid_values)) {
    return(output)
  }

  if (max(x[valid_values]) >= 30) {

    output[valid_values] <- sprintf(
      "%.1f",
      x[valid_values]
    )

  } else {

    output[valid_values] <- format(
      x[valid_values],
      trim = TRUE,
      scientific = FALSE
    )
  }

  output
}


############################################################
# 15) Shared plot theme
############################################################

sequencing_theme <- theme_bw(
  base_size = 9
) +
  theme(
    panel.background = element_rect(
      fill = "white",
      colour = NA
    ),

    panel.grid.major.y = element_line(
      colour = "#E5E5E5",
      linewidth = 0.35
    ),

    panel.grid.minor.y = element_line(
      colour = "#F2F2F2",
      linewidth = 0.25
    ),

    panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.minor.x = element_blank(),

    panel.border = element_rect(
      fill = NA,
      colour = "#4D4D4D",
      linewidth = 0.55
    ),

    strip.background = element_rect(
      fill = "#F2F2F2",
      colour = "#7A7A7A",
      linewidth = 0.45
    ),

    strip.text = element_text(
      colour = "black",
      face = "bold",
      size = 7.5,
      margin = margin(
        t = 2,
        r = 2,
        b = 2,
        l = 2
      )
    ),

    axis.title = element_text(
      colour = "black",
      face = "bold",
      size = 9
    ),

    axis.text = element_text(
      colour = "#333333",
      size = 7.5
    ),

    axis.text.x = element_text(
      angle = 90,
      hjust = 1,
      vjust = 0.5
    ),

    axis.ticks = element_line(
      colour = "#4D4D4D",
      linewidth = 0.35
    ),

    axis.ticks.length = grid::unit(
      2,
      "pt"
    ),

    plot.title = element_text(
      colour = "black",
      face = "bold",
      size = 10,
      hjust = 0,
      margin = margin(
        b = 4
      )
    ),

    panel.spacing.y = grid::unit(
      0.10,
      "cm"
    ),

    legend.title = element_blank(),

    legend.text = element_text(
      colour = "black",
      size = 7.5
    ),

    legend.key = element_rect(
      fill = "white",
      colour = NA
    ),

    legend.key.width = grid::unit(
      14,
      "pt"
    ),

    legend.key.height = grid::unit(
      10,
      "pt"
    ),

    legend.spacing.x = grid::unit(
      3,
      "pt"
    ),

    legend.margin = margin(
      t = 0,
      r = 0,
      b = 0,
      l = 0
    ),

    plot.margin = margin(
      t = 3,
      r = 4,
      b = 3,
      l = 4
    )
  )


# Hide sampling-date labels in the first three sections.
hide_sampling_dates <- theme(
  axis.text.x = element_blank(),
  axis.ticks.x = element_blank(),
  axis.title.x = element_blank()
)


############################################################
# 16) Read-count plot
############################################################

Read_Counts_Plot <- ggplot(
  read_count_bar_data,
  aes(
    x = Sampling_Date_Label,
    y = Value,
    fill = Technology,
    alpha = Filtering_Status
  )
) +
  geom_col(
    width = 0.80,
    colour = "#333333",
    linewidth = 0.25
  ) +
  scale_fill_manual(
    values = technology_colours,
    breaks = technology_levels,
    drop = FALSE,
    na.translate = FALSE
  ) +
  scale_alpha_manual(
    values = filtering_alpha,
    breaks = filtering_levels,
    drop = FALSE,
    na.translate = FALSE
  ) +
  scale_x_discrete(
    drop = FALSE,
    expand = expansion(
      add = c(0.50, 0.50)
    )
  ) +
  scale_y_continuous(
    breaks = read_count_breaks,
    labels = format_read_counts,
    expand = expansion(
      mult = c(0, 0.05)
    )
  ) +
  facet_wrap(
    vars(Technology),
    ncol = 1,
    scales = "free_y"
  ) +
  guides(
    fill = guide_legend(
      order = 1,
      override.aes = list(
        alpha = 1,
        colour = "#555555",
        linewidth = 0.35
      )
    ),

    alpha = guide_legend(
      order = 2,
      override.aes = list(
        fill = "#808080",
        colour = "#555555",
        linewidth = 0.35
      )
    )
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Read counts",
    x = NULL,
    y = "Number of reads",
    fill = NULL,
    alpha = NULL
  ) +
  sequencing_theme +
  hide_sampling_dates

############################################################
# 18) Mean-read-length plot
############################################################

Mean_Read_Length_Plot <- ggplot(
  mean_read_length_data,
  aes(
    x = Sampling_Date_Label,
    y = Value
  )
) +
  geom_segment(
    data = sequencing_wide,
    aes(
      x = Sampling_Date_Label,
      xend = Sampling_Date_Label,
      y = Mean_Read_Length_Raw,
      yend = Mean_Read_Length_Processed,
      colour = Technology
    ),
    inherit.aes = FALSE,
    linewidth = 0.35,
    alpha = 0.35,
    show.legend = FALSE
  ) +
  geom_point(
    aes(
      colour = Technology,
      alpha = Processing
    ),
    size = 1.8
  ) +
  scale_colour_manual(
    values = technology_colours,
    breaks = technology_levels,
    drop = FALSE,
    na.translate = FALSE
  ) +
  scale_alpha_manual(
    values = processing_alpha,
    breaks = processing_levels,
    drop = FALSE,
    na.translate = FALSE
  ) +
  scale_x_discrete(
    drop = FALSE,
    expand = expansion(
      add = c(0.50, 0.50)
    )
  ) +
  scale_y_continuous(
    breaks = mean_read_length_breaks,
    labels = format_read_length,
    expand = expansion(
      mult = c(0.07, 0.07)
    )
  ) +
  facet_wrap(
    vars(Technology),
    ncol = 1,
    scales = "free_y"
  ) +
  guides(
    alpha = guide_legend(
      order = 3,
      override.aes = list(
        colour = "#666666",
        size = 1.8
      )
    ),

    colour = guide_legend(
      order = 4,
      override.aes = list(
        alpha = 1,
        size = 1.8
      )
    )
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Mean read length",
    x = NULL,
    y = "Mean read length (bp)",
    colour = NULL,
    alpha = NULL
  ) +
  sequencing_theme +
  hide_sampling_dates


############################################################
# 19) Mean-read-quality plot
############################################################

Mean_Read_Quality_Plot <- ggplot(
  mean_read_quality_data,
  aes(
    x = Sampling_Date_Label,
    y = Value
  )
) +
  geom_segment(
    data = sequencing_wide,
    aes(
      x = Sampling_Date_Label,
      xend = Sampling_Date_Label,
      y = Mean_Read_Quality_Raw,
      yend = Mean_Read_Quality_Processed,
      colour = Technology
    ),
    inherit.aes = FALSE,
    linewidth = 0.35,
    alpha = 0.35,
    show.legend = FALSE
  ) +
  geom_point(
    aes(
      colour = Technology,
      alpha = Processing
    ),
    size = 1.8
  ) +
  scale_colour_manual(
    values = technology_colours,
    breaks = technology_levels,
    drop = FALSE,
    na.translate = FALSE
  ) +
  scale_alpha_manual(
    values = processing_alpha,
    breaks = processing_levels,
    drop = FALSE,
    na.translate = FALSE
  ) +
  scale_x_discrete(
    drop = FALSE,
    expand = expansion(
      add = c(0.50, 0.50)
    )
  ) +
  scale_y_continuous(
    breaks = scales::breaks_pretty(
      n = 5
    ),
    labels = format_read_quality,
    expand = expansion(
      mult = c(0.07, 0.07)
    )
  ) +
  facet_wrap(
    vars(Technology),
    ncol = 1,
    scales = "free_y"
  ) +
  guides(
    alpha = guide_legend(
      order = 3,
      override.aes = list(
        colour = "#666666",
        size = 1.8
      )
    ),

    colour = guide_legend(
      order = 4,
      override.aes = list(
        alpha = 1,
        size = 1.8
      )
    )
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Mean read quality",
    x = "Sampling date",
    y = "Mean read quality (Phred Q score)",
    colour = NULL,
    alpha = NULL
  ) +
  sequencing_theme


############################################################
# 20) Combine the four sections
############################################################

Sequencing_Performance_Overview <- (
  Read_Counts_Plot /
    Sequencing_Yield_Plot /
    Mean_Read_Length_Plot /
    Mean_Read_Quality_Plot
) +
  plot_layout(
    heights = c(
      1,
      1,
      1,
      1.15
    ),
    guides = "collect"
  )


############################################################
# 21) Place the collected legends at the top
############################################################

Sequencing_Performance_Overview <-
  Sequencing_Performance_Overview &
  theme(
    legend.position = "top",
    legend.direction = "horizontal",
    legend.box = "horizontal",
    legend.box.just = "center"
  )


############################################################
# 22) Display the completed figure
############################################################

print(
  Sequencing_Performance_Overview
)

ggsave(
  filename = "Sequencing_Performance_Overview_A4.png",
  plot = Sequencing_Performance_Overview,
  device = "png",
  width = 210,
  height = 297,
  units = "mm",
  dpi = 600,
  bg = "white"
)
```

```{r}
# ============================================================
# Source data export: Supplementary Figure 10
# One row = one date × technology × processing state
# ============================================================

base_dir <- paste0(
  "C:/SynologyDrive/PhD/Projects/SpringBloom2021/",
  "DataAnalysis_SpringBloom2021"
)

source_dir <- file.path(
  base_dir,
  "Source_Data_Supplement"
)

dir.create(
  source_dir,
  recursive = TRUE,
  showWarnings = FALSE
)

suppl_figure_10 <- sequencing_data |>
  dplyr::transmute(
    Sample = as.character(Sample),
    Sampling_Date = as.Date(Sampling_Date),
    Sequencing_Technology = as.character(Technology),
    Processing_State = as.character(Processing),
    Number_Of_Reads = as.numeric(Number_Of_Reads),
    Sequencing_Yield_Gbp = as.numeric(Total_Bases) / 1e9,
    Mean_Read_Length_bp = as.numeric(Mean_Read_Length),
    Mean_Read_Quality_Phred = as.numeric(Mean_Read_Quality)
  ) |>
  dplyr::arrange(
    Sampling_Date,
    Sequencing_Technology,
    Processing_State
  )

readr::write_excel_csv(
  suppl_figure_10,
  file.path(source_dir, "Suppl_Figure_10.csv"),
  na = ""
)
```
